section: Navigation satellites - IRNSS/NavIC constellation and GAGAN; applications and limitations

accepted.s: The failure of the clock in which satellite was associated with the reduction of the operational NavIC constellation to three working satellites on 13 March 2026?
o: IRNSS-1F
IRNSS-1G
IRNSS-1A
IRNSS-1D
accepted.x: The reduction of the working NavIC constellation was attributed to the clock failure in IRNSS-1F.
accepted.tq: Identify the satellite directly linked with the stated technical failure.

accepted.s: On 13 March 2026, the NavIC constellation was reported to have how many working satellites?
o: Three
Seven
Five
Four
accepted.x: Following the IRNSS-1F clock failure, only three NavIC satellites were reported to be working.
accepted.tq: Read the numerical value carefully and distinguish the current operational count from the full constellation.

accepted.s: What immediate course of action was urged in relation to NavIC before the next NVS launches?
o: Fixing the existing system’s operational issues
Replacing NavIC with GPS for civilian use
Restricting NavIC to military applications only
Decommissioning the remaining working satellites
accepted.x: ISRO was urged to address the problems affecting NavIC before proceeding with the next NVS launches.
accepted.tq: Match the stated problem with the corresponding institutional response.

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): NavIC is important for India’s strategic autonomy.
Reason (R): During a conflict, Indian forces and emergency responders need not depend entirely on foreign navigation systems when an indigenous system is available.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. Reduced dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict directly explains NavIC’s importance for strategic autonomy.
accepted.tq: Test whether the Reason explains the strategic significance stated in the Assertion.

accepted.s: GPS jamming reported near the Strait of Hormuz during the West Asia conflict most directly illustrates which risk?
o: The restriction of satellite navigation to maritime transport
The complete failure of all regional navigation systems
The inability of satellites to provide weather information
The vulnerability created by dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict
accepted.x: GPS jamming near the Strait of Hormuz illustrates the operational risk of relying on foreign navigation systems in a conflict situation.
accepted.tq: Apply the strategic-autonomy concept to a conflict-related navigation disruption.

accepted.s: NavIC-based alerts are of particular practical importance to Andhra Pradesh because they assist which group during cyclones?
o: Mountain rescue teams in the Eastern Himalayas
航空 traffic controllers at international airports
Only inland agricultural labourers
Fishermen operating along the long coastline
accepted.x: NavIC-based fishermen alerts can support the large fishing community along Andhra Pradesh’s long coastline during cyclones.
accepted.tq: Link the regional application with the geographic feature and affected community.
